title: SLO-aware adaptive shard coordinator for embeddings ingress
creator: Rahul Singh
description:
Problem: We observe repeated spike-driven p99 tail latency on the embeddings endpoint during multi-tenant bursts. Root causes include: head-of-line blocking from large tenant batches, single-shard hot keys, inefficient admission control that is blind to configured SLOs, and over-aggressive autoscaler actions that oscillate. Impact: high-latency client errors and throttling for latency-sensitive customers (search/rerank pipelines).

Goal: Implement an SLO-aware adaptive shard coordinator + front-line admission controller to: (1) enforce tenant-specific latency SLOs, (2) avoid global queue head-of-line blocking, (3) provide smoother autoscaling signals, and (4) reduce p99 by at least 2x under mixed workloads while retaining or improving overall throughput.

High-level approach: Build a lightweight coordinator service that: 1) maintains per-tenant and per-shard admission state (max concurrency, leaky-bucket rate) derived from tenant SLOs and measured tail latencies; 2) performs weighted fair-queueing across tenants within each embedding shard; 3) exposes backpressure headers (X-RW-Backoff) to SDKs/routers and an admission API for the router to consult; 4) emits stable autoscaler signals (smoothed active_concurrency_per_shard) that the autoscaler consumes instead of raw queue depth; 5) supports warm-pool reservations for pinned tenants and fast-path routing for cached prefixes.

Why this design: Centralized coordination lets us reason about tenant SLOs and global fairness (alternative: fully-local heuristics in each shard were tried in prototypes and failed to prevent cascading drops). Weighted fair-queueing prevents a single noisy tenant from starving others. Moving to SLO-derived admission (instead of fixed rate-limits) lets us prioritize latency-sensitive customers while permitting best-effort throughput for bulk jobs. Emitting smoothed concurrency metrics reduces autoscaler thrash versus reacting to short-lived queue spikes.

Trade-offs and constraints: - Coordinator introduces an extra network hop and slightly higher request ingress path complexity; mitigated by lightweight in-RAM state and co-locating coordinator replicas in the same VPC subnet as routers. - Centralized state must be highly-available; we will run small leaderless consensus using existing placement manager (etcd-backed) with read-replicas for routers. - Tuning complexity: per-tenant SLO translation to admission policy requires sensible defaults and a learning window.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Under mixed tenant synthetic workload (70% small low-latency tenants, 30% high-throughput bulk tenants) the embedding p99 across tenants drops by >= 50% compared to baseline and p95 improves by >= 25%.
2) No increase in overall embedding request failures (>0.5% HTTP 5xx) during 1h canary.
3) Autoscaler signal variance (stdev of active_concurrency_per_shard over 5m windows) reduced by >= 35%.
4) SDKs receive X-RW-Backoff headers during enforced backpressure; at least one SDK integration test exercises retry/backoff.
5) Rollout plan completed (canary -> region roll -> global) with documented rollback steps and runbook).
tech_notes:
Implementation components: 
- Coordinator service (Go) with gRPC admission API and lightweight in-memory per-tenant state (LRU eviction for infrequent tenants).
- Router integration: consult admission API before enqueue; include backpressure header propagation.
- Shard-local fair-queue: token-leaky bucket + deficit-round-robin weights for tenants.
- Autoscaler integration: export smoothed_active_concurrency_per_shard (EMA alpha=0.1 and 60s window) to metric 'embeddings.coordinator.active_concurrency'.
- Config: tenant SLOs are read from tenant profiles (default latency SLO=200ms for latency tier customers).
- Persisted knobs: per-tenant max-burst, min-reservation, priority weight.

Data models and algorithms: 
- Admission decision = allow if current_inflight < tenant_max_concurrency AND global_shard_headroom > shard_reserved_headroom_for_priority.
- Tenant_max_concurrency is computed from SLO target and observed p95 latency via hill-climbing with a conservative decrease factor.

Benchmarks (local): Prototype reduced p99 in lab from 420ms -> 160ms under 3x burst traffic; throughput preserved within 5%. We will run k6-based distributed harness for more exhaustive numbers.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged coordinator deployed to staging with routers pointing to staging coordinator (2 weeks of soak).
2) Canary in us-west-2: 5% traffic, monitor p50/p95/p99, error rate, autoscaler signal for 48h.
3) Expand to 25% for 24h, 50% for 24h, then full region.
4) Repeat per region with scheduled windows.
5) Post-rollout: enable warm-pool reservations for top-20 tenants by traffic in a phased manner.

Rollback: disable coordinator flag on routers -> routers fall back to local best-effort admission. Coordinator supports graceful shutdown draining with 60s drain window.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: embeddings.coordinator.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, embeddings.coordinator.queue_length, embeddings.coordinator.drop_rate, embeddings.coordinator.active_concurrency, embeddings.coordinator.autoscaler_signal_variance.
Alerts: p99 > baseline*1.5 for 10m OR drop_rate > 1% OR autoscaler_thrash_detected -> page on-call infra.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for admission logic and weight scheduling.
- Integration tests: router + coordinator interaction w/ mocked shards.
- Load tests in perf lab: burst mix, cold-warm pool transitions, hot-tenant scenarios.
- Chaos testing: kill coordinator replica, network partitioning, autoscaler delay injection.
- SDK test: verify X-RW-Backoff header handling and exponential backoff behavior.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: coordinator single-point-of-failure causing large outage. Mitigation: run N+2 replicas, health-check circuit-breaker in router, fallback to local admission if coordinator unavailable.
Risk: misconfiguration causing under-provisioning for bulk customers. Mitigation: staged rollout, traffic shaping and canary thresholds, telemetry dashboards for immediate reconfiguration.
